schema.description: A change of dose within a medicine course, one row in the med.regimen series. Written into records files by hand, by reading My Health Record dispensing screenshots or from the person's own word.

as_dispensed.description: The pharmacy dispense record as the source shows it: the product line (generic name with the maker in brackets, or the brand, then form and strength) and the directions, joined by a comma. Verbatim but for the directions' first letter, written lower case.
examples: EXAMPLAZOLE (XYZ) TAB 20mg, take ONE tablet daily

course.description: Which course of this drug, counting from 1; a restart after a stop is a new course. Assigned by whoever wrote the record, not by the source. With drug it names the regimen series.

date.description: The day of the change, YYYY-MM-DD. For My Health Record rows, the dispensing date the screenshot shows. This is the fact time.

dispensed_at.description: The dispensing pharmacy's name, as the source shows it.

dose.description: The new dose the reader worked out from the first dispense line at it: its strength times the tablets per day in the directions, with the unit and frequency in words. The reader's summary, not the source's text. Whether it means the prescribed dose when tablets of another strength are dispensed is not settled.

drug.description: The generic drug name in lower case, as the record's writer normalised it from the source. With course it names the regimen series.

id.description: Identity, chosen by the writer: the source prefix, then med, the drug, the course, "dose-changed" and the date.

prescribed_by.description: The prescriber named on the prescription, as shown.

source_note.description: What the reader saw in the source and how they reached this record (which screenshot, which dispensing). Reader's text, not the source's.
